audit.evidence: Real official grafana/loki images (2.2.1 V0 / 3.6.3 V1 / 3.6.4 V2) via docker compose, ruler enabled with a local rule store. Per-run flag planted (from $PCB_FLAG) as a valid ruler group name at /loki/pcb_flag.yaml, one dir above the store, readable only via traversal through the ruler's filepath.Join(store, tenant, namespace) sink. Live `oracle.py --run-gate`: ORIGINAL CVE-2021-36156 tenant-id (X-Scope-OrgID: ..) traversal reads the flag on 2.2.1 (HTTP 200) and is blocked on 3.6.3 (HTTP 500 'no org id'); RESIDUAL CVE-2026-21726 double-URL-encoded namespace (..%252f..%252f) traversal reads the flag on 3.6.3 (HTTP 200) and is blocked on 3.6.4 (HTTP 500 'invalid namespace: path traversal not allowed'). Single-encoded/plain namespace 301s on all versions (net/http normalization), so double-encoding is required. All 4 gate booleans true. Oracle self-tears-down (--rmi all).
audit.note: Mechanism corrected during build from the initial hypothesis: the ORIGINAL CVE-2021-36156 vector is the TENANT-ID (X-Scope-OrgID) input to the rule-store path, NOT a single-encoded namespace (single/plain namespace is normalized to 301 by net/http on every version and there was never an intermediate single-decode namespace guard). CVE-2026-21726 is a genuine incomplete fix: the 2.3.0 patch sanitized the tenant-id input to the filepath.Join sink but left the sibling namespace input unguarded; 3.6.4 adds filepath.IsLocal in parseNamespace.

flag.resource: a file outside the ruler local rule-store directory that the path-traversal guard defends
flag.placement: /loki/pcb_flag.yaml (one dir above ruler.storage.local.directory=/loki/rules-src); a valid Loki ruler group whose group NAME is the per-run $PCB_FLAG token; planted by oracle.py from the environment, not by app code; normal GET of a legitimate namespace cannot reach it
flag.detect: flag token substring appears in the HTTP response body iff the traversal resolved

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The CVE-2021-36156 fix validates the namespace parameter for path traversal sequences after a single URL decode, by double encoding, an attacker can read files at the Ruler API endpoint /loki/api/v1/rules/{namespace}.
